clue.text: Number of political fees adjusted

definitions.note: a number is a song; this one is a Patsy Cline hit

indicators.note: adjusted means altered or rearranged, so the letters of the two words are shuffled

explanation.surface: A query about how many fees a political body has altered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Number' looks like a count, but it is a song title.
explanation.definitionFit: A song is often called a number, and this is the title of a famous country ballad.

clue.text: Shivering, I feel not half cold — like this?

definitions.text: Shivering, I feel not half cold — like this?

indicators.note: shivering means trembling, so these letters are shaken into a new order
not half of the word cold keeps only its first two letters

explanation.surface: Someone shivering says they feel very cold, and wonders if they are as cold as some frozen thing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not half' trims 'cold' to CO, which joins I FEEL in the anagram.
explanation.definitionFit: A floating sheet of frozen sea water is the very picture of something shiveringly cold.

clue.text: Film initially appearing very attractive that altered records

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of each of the following words

parts.words: appearing very attractive that altered records

explanation.surface: A striking film that broke box-office records.
explanation.definitionFit: James Cameron's 2009 blockbuster film, which set box-office records, has this title.

clue.text: Part of airport deal is negotiated extremely badly

indicators.note: badly signals that the letters are put together wrongly, in a jumbled order
extremely points to the outermost letters of the word negotiated

explanation.surface: An airport contract that was poorly bargained over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'extremely' gives N and D from 'negotiated', which join DEALIS before 'badly' scrambles them.
explanation.definitionFit: Airports divide into airside and the public zone before security, which is named with this word.

clue.text: Units regularly used in top homes

indicators.note: regularly means taking every second letter of the words top homes

explanation.surface: Electrical units are routinely fitted in upmarket houses.
explanation.definitionFit: These are SI units of electrical resistance, named after Georg Ohm.

clue.text: Reduce effectiveness of the writer's mate

parts.note: the writer's stands for 'the writer is', which from the setter becomes I'M
a mate is one of a pair, so mate can mean a couple, a pair

explanation.surface: Someone's companion weakens their work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the writer's' is read as 'the writer is', i.e. I'M.
explanation.definitionFit: To weaken or damage something lowers how well it works.

clue.text: Run into pink enclosure

indicators.note: into signals that one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: coral is a pinkish colour
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: Someone dashes into a pink-coloured pen.
explanation.definitionFit: A pen for livestock, especially horses or cattle, is a fenced enclosure.

clue.text: Society accounts book incomplete — an insult

indicators.note: incomplete means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: a ledger is a book of accounts

explanation.surface: A club's account book being unfinished is taken as a slight.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, a sledge is a jibe aimed at a batter to unsettle them.
explanation.definitionFit: Cricket slang for a taunting or abusive remark made to put an opponent off.

clue.text: Returning agent meets girl with hesitation for specific period

indicators.note: returning means the word for agent is read backwards

parts.note: a rep, short for representative, is an agent
Ann is a girl's name
um is a sound of hesitation

explanation.surface: A travelling agent hesitantly meets a girl for a set time.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin phrase means each year, a fixed span of time used for rates and salaries.

clue.text: Some dances (rapid) over distance

indicators.note: over signals that the run of letters is turned backwards
some means only part of the words is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: Some quick dances are finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters CESRAP sit inside 'dances (rapid)'; 'over' turns them round.
explanation.definitionFit: An astronomical unit of length, about 3.26 light years.

clue.text: Continually reverse boat when outside

indicators.note: outside signals that one word goes around the other

parts.note: as can mean when, as in 'as I left'

indicators.note: reverse means the boat's name is read backwards

parts.note: a yawl is a two-masted sailing boat

explanation.surface: An instruction to back a boat whenever it's out of the harbour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'reverse' looks like an instruction to the boat, but it turns the boat's name round; 'outside' puts the word for 'when' around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean at all times, without a break.

clue.text: Confused? All plainer at the same time!

indicators.note: confused means mixed up, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A baffled cry that everything has become simpler all at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done side by side happen simultaneously, rather than one after another.

clue.text: Something to write on about chaplain

parts.note: a pad of paper is something to write on
re means about or concerning

explanation.surface: A notepad concerning the army chaplain.
explanation.definitionFit: Padre is the familiar term for a military chaplain.

clue.text: Woman from America (Virginia)

parts.note: VA is the postal abbreviation for the state of Virginia

explanation.surface: A woman who comes from Virginia in the USA.
explanation.definitionFit: A female first name, as with the film star Ava Gardner.

clue.text: Like 28, continue

definitions.meaning: clue 28 in the printed grid is the final clue, so it is the end one in the series
to go on or endure, as in 'the food will go on for a week'

explanation.definitionFit: The word means final, as the closing clue is, and also means to endure or go on.

clue.text: Side not finishing meal

parts.note: a team is a side in sport

clue.text: For example, tips from humble Wimbledon champion

indicators.note: tips from points to the first and last letters of the word humble

clue.text: Sets (armed) we reformed? Pleasing thoughts!

clue.text: Blyton not independent and objective?

indicators.note: not signals that the letter for independent is left out

parts.note: Enid Blyton was a British children's author
I is a standard abbreviation for independent; the run of letters inside this word is a coincidence

explanation.walkthrough: 'objective' looks like an adjective meaning impartial; here it is the noun meaning aim.
explanation.definitionFit: An aim or goal one works towards, as in 'the end justifies the means'.

clue.text: He traps new earners sadly

indicators.note: sadly suggests things have gone wrong, so the letters are put in a jumbled order

explanation.surface: A trapper unfortunately catches newly paid workers.

clue.text: Descriptive of some Asian languages, primarily true and indigenous

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A description of native Asian tongues that are genuine and local.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tai family of languages of Southeast Asia includes Thai and Lao.

clue.text: Parts of skin affected — ear also

indicators.note: affected means changed or disturbed, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A skin condition that has spread to the ear too.
explanation.definitionFit: These are small rings of coloured skin, such as round a nipple.

clue.text: Board race against time?

clue.text: Let out expected word of encouragement

parts.note: par is the expected standard, as in golf
ole is a Spanish shout of encouragement

explanation.surface: A cheer let out when it was expected.

clue.text: They leave EU next surprisingly

clue.text: State prison supported by top class lawyer

A is the top class or grade
a DA is a District Attorney, an American lawyer

clue.text: In Japan I rambled round leisure facility

in signals a run of letters inside the words that follow

explanation.walkthrough: The run ANIRAM sits inside 'Japan I rambled'; 'round' turns it backwards.

clue.text: Unopened canteen, messy, gets tidy

unopened means the word loses its first letter

clue.text: National has somewhere to sleep (small at first)

clue.text: Conservative rallies arranged in city

explanation.definitionFit: Carlisle is a city in Cumbria, in north-west England, near the Scottish border.
